trust_decision.summary: Before anything is created, createFile canonicalises the whole member path and requires it to start with the canonical destination + separator; but makeFile then mkdir()s every literal '/'-split prefix of that same name, so a prefix such as '../extract_evil/../extract' is created outside the root even though the full path canonicalises back inside and passes the check.

landing_point.why: The summary names mkdir escape; makeFile (lines 75-94) is the only place in src/main that calls mkdir(), and its per-prefix loop is the code that creates directories.

fix_sites.entry_point: Junrar.extract(...) public static API: File/File, InputStream/File and VolumeManager/File (each with an optional password), all constructing LocalFolderExtractor and calling extract(Archive, FileHeader)
fix_sites.module_kind: core library, single Gradle module (src/main/java), package com.github.junrar

fix_sites.entry_point: same public API; all overloads converge on createFile -> makeFile, so this is the single site the check must hold at
fix_sites.module_kind: core library, single Gradle module (src/main/java), package com.github.junrar

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exist; the only dismissal worth recording is the one a solver could try on Archive.extractFile(FileHeader, OutputStream) (src/main/java/com/github/junrar/Archive.java:575) - 'that lower-level API writes decompressed bytes to a caller-supplied stream, so path safety is the caller's job' - which is true, but that API never touches the filesystem, so it is not a route into this sink.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The existing rejection contract must stay (IllegalStateException whose message names the canonical offending path) while legitimate nested members must still get their parent directories created and be returned as extracted entries (test.rar's foo/bar.txt -> foo/ exists and appears in the result list). An over-broad rewrite - rejecting any name that contains '..', or swapping in Paths.get()/InvalidPathException or a different message - breaks these tests.

O6_input_shapes: multi-component '/'-separated member names (nested paths, the only shape that reaches the mkdir loop)
names whose components include '.' or '..' (Path.normalize collapses them lexically so only the validated final path is materialised)
single-component names, where no directory has to be created
names where an intermediate '..' prefix resolves outside the root while the full path canonicalises back inside (the reported shape, e.g. '../extract_evil/../extract/f')
backslash-separated names, converted to '/' by invariantSeparatorsPathString before both the check and the creation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a createDirectory(FileHeader) that actually materialises the directory (today it only validates and returns the File, so an archive holding only directory entries extracts nothing)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RAR stores explicit directory entries and users expect empty directories to be recreated; a maintainer adding that would reuse the same final-path-only canonical check and call File.mkdir(), recreating the escape in a second sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sibling extraction wrapper that also restores unix owners, EAs or symlinks straight from the header (UnixOwnersHeader/EAHeader are already parsed) and writes to a path it builds from the header name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Junrar.tryToExtract already dispatches on header kind; attribute-preserving extraction is a natural next feature and would build paths from the same helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an extractFile(FileHeader, File) convenience overload that derives the target file from fh.getFileName()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: README.md:66-77 documents the stream form; users repeatedly ask for the File form, and such an overload would need its own copy of the destination check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a real filename validator in the parser (isFilenameValid today only checks that new File(name).getCanonicalPath() does not throw, i.e. it validates nothing) applied when the header is read
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The name is attacker-controlled at parse time and the helper already exists with a validating name; tightening it is an obvious 'defence in depth' change a maintainer could write.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal / zip-slip - directory creation outside the extraction root

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 9.5.1 wrapper (build.gradle:165-168), java-library plugin, dependencies from Maven Central (slf4j-api, JUnit Jupiter 5.9.1, AssertJ, Mockito, ArchUnit, commons-io); no annotation processing needed for normal builds
O10_build.project_tests: src/test/java/com/github/junrar/LocalFolderExtractorTest.java (canonical-path rejection unit tests, incl. the existing sibling-prefix-traversal.rar case), src/test/java/com/github/junrar/JunrarTest.java (happy-day nested extraction), plus a separate regressionTest JvmTestSuite over src/regressionTest/resources run via 'gradle regressionTest' (tag 'check')

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the split/mkdir loop with Files.createDirectories(f.toPath().getParent()) without calling Path.normalize(): createDirectories recurses on the lexical getParent() chain, so it still mkdirs '<root>/extract_evil' through the '..' segment and the escape survives.

out_of_scope_notes: src/main/java/com/github/junrar/rarfile/FileHeader.java:230-237 isFilenameValid() canonicalises the name in the JVM working directory and only rejects names whose getCanonicalPath() throws, so it validates nothing - an adjacent weakness in the parser layer, not a route into this advisory's sink and not touched by the fix.
unverified: The exact member name inside the fix's src/test/resources/com/github/junrar/mkdir-escape.rar - it is binary and unreadable here; the escaping shape is inferred from the test's assertions (root.resolve("extract_evil") must not exist while the extraction itself must not throw) and from makeFile.

Whether java.io.File.getCanonicalPath() collapses '..' that follows a non-existent component on the grading JDK; the escape does not depend on it (a returning path such as '../extract_evil/../extract/f' passes the check either way), but it decides whether any pure file-write route also escapes without directory creation.
Whether the three archive-source families (eight public overloads) should be counted as 3 entry points or 1 API; j_multi_site follows the stated O1 >= 2 rule.
